## Public core boundary

Web consumers import only the core entry point, `packages/core/index.ts`; storage remains behind it. Core may use its own storage internals. Dependencies must be acyclic. There are no boundary or cycle exceptions.
The existing `packages/web/public.ts` is a representative public consumer:

```ts
import { price } from '../core/index.ts'
export function quote() { return price() }
```

Public quote remains 12. The controlled HTTP endpoint in `journey.mjs` supplies price 10; checkout must return status 201 and total 10. No new discount or receipt wording is selected.
`boundaries.mjs` uses TypeScript resolution for static imports, re-exports, import types, import-equals and literal dynamic imports. Nonliteral dynamic imports and require calls are rejected because their dependency cannot be established.

## Completing and maintaining a change

Use Node 24 or later and the lockfile-pinned TypeScript toolchain. Set up with `npm ci`; run `npm run check` for types, native boundaries, public unit checks and the real loopback HTTP checkout journey. Acceptance cases live here and in `journey.mjs` and `unit.test.mjs`. A change is complete when its affected journeys pass on final inputs; passing unit tests alone does not establish completion.

`.bstack/project.json` maps changed paths to this design, `glossary.md`, agent pointers, rules and required leaf checks. For each change, compare against an explicit ancestor base; assess every mapped document and unmapped path against literal base/current sources. Record substantive updates, concrete no-impact reasoning or blocked owner decisions. Review the live diff before binding the assessment fingerprint. New failures must fail checks; do not add blanket exclusions or silently accept new debt.

For portable review, commit implementation first, collect and review `.bstack/assessment.json`, bind its fingerprint, then commit the assessment separately. The assessment retains the implementation head and only that assessment may change afterwards. Use the repo-owned command helpers to collect and validate:

```sh
node .bstack/bin/repo-audit.mjs evidence collect --repo . --base <ancestor-commit> --portable .bstack/assessment.json --json
node .bstack/bin/repo-audit.mjs evidence validate --repo . --base <ancestor-commit> --assessment .bstack/assessment.json --json
node .bstack/bin/bstack-check.mjs --repo . --base <ancestor-commit> --assessment .bstack/assessment.json --json
```

The last command executes required checks freshly. Run it in the working checkout and a different-root clean clone with isolated home/cache and the same base and committed assessment. Dependency installation remains an explicit prerequisite. No hosted CI or delivery service is selected.

The first maintenance contract is selected foundation F-005. Future changes must retain previous policy coverage or obtain explicit migration approval. Repo-owned checker/runtime and schema files are copied from the complete installed repo-audit package; the standalone gate requires Node and Git without an agent session. Review authority changes independently of passing checks.

`docs/repo-audit.md` is a historical snapshot with its observed revision, not a live readiness authority. Keep current-head findings, checker captures and readiness in scratch; do not rewrite the snapshot after each run.
